articles.title: India Summons Air India CEO After Phuket Flight's Sudden Altitude Loss
articles.excerpt: Civil aviation ministry calls in Campbell Wilson as pilot drug test results and Airbus specialists add new layers to the probe into last week's mid-air scare.
articles.nri_angle: Air India is India's flagship carrier and a primary airline for the Indian diaspora traveling between India and international destinations. Safety incidents on its routes directly affect NRI travelers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh Student Dileep Kumar Bungatavula Killed in Ohio After Pick-Up Truck Rams His Car Head-On
articles.excerpt: The North America Telugu Society has launched a fundraiser to support the student's farming family back in Andhra Pradesh, adding to a grim toll of Indian student road fatalities in the US.
articles.image_caption: The Prentice Memorial Gateway at Kent State University in Kent, Ohio. Dileep Kumar Bungatavula, a student from Andhra Pradesh based in Kent, was killed in a head-on collision with a pick-up truck.
articles.nri_angle: Indian student from Andhra Pradesh killed in Ohio; Telugu diaspora organizations mobilize fundraising for his farming family.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Judge Dismisses Criminal Charges Against Gautam Adani After DOJ Abandons Bribery Case
articles.excerpt: Brooklyn federal judge grants rare DOJ request to drop 2024 fraud and bribery indictment, ending a high-profile prosecution that spanned two presidential administrations.
articles.image_caption: Gautam Adani, chairman of the Adani Group. A US federal judge dismissed criminal bribery charges against Adani on Monday after the Department of Justice moved to abandon the case.
articles.nri_angle: The dismissal of charges against India's second-richest person removes a cloud over Adani Group's US investment plans and signals a shift in how American courts handle cross-border corporate cases.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Flash Floods Rip Apart Bridge in Uttarakhand's Niti Valley, BRO Driver Missing
articles.excerpt: A violent flash flood in Chamoli district swept away a bridge and a vehicle on the Jyotirmath-Malari highway, cutting off over a dozen border villages as monsoon fury continues across the state.
articles.image_caption: A footbridge destroyed by floodwaters over the Mandakini river in Uttarakhand. Flash floods in Chamoli district ripped apart a bridge on the Jyotirmath-Malari highway, cutting off villages in the Niti Valley.
articles.nri_angle: The Niti Valley bridge collapse disrupts a key route to Hindu pilgrimage sites near Badrinath, affecting NRI travelers planning Char Dham yatra during the monsoon season.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Explosive Drone at German Airport and Bulgaria Blast Raise NATO Security Alarm
articles.excerpt: An armed drone found near Ukrainian cargo planes at Leipzig/Halle Airport and a separate explosion in Bulgarian airspace expose growing vulnerabilities in Europe's defence against unmanned aerial threats.
articles.image_caption: Police officers stand near a Ukrainian Antonov cargo plane at Leipzig/Halle Airport after an explosive-laden drone was discovered on August 5, 2026. German federal prosecutors have launched a terrorism investigation into the incident.
articles.nri_angle: NATO drone incidents highlight growing security threats across Europe, with implications for global stability and diaspora communities monitoring the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Tells Meta to Follow Indian Law, Not Just Its Own Global Policies
articles.excerpt: The Indian government has told Meta that its platforms must comply with the country's laws and cannot operate solely under the company's internal global policies, following weeks of escalating confrontations over content moderation failures.
articles.image_caption: A graphic showing the Indian government and Meta logos. India has told Meta it must comply with Indian law, not just its own global content policies.
articles.nri_angle: Stricter regulation of Meta's platforms in India could reshape how NRIs use WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook to connect with family and communities in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: North Korean Missile Unit Deploys to Russia With Up to 120 Ballistic Missiles for Ukraine Strikes
articles.excerpt: Ukrainian intelligence says about 90 North Korean personnel are setting up in Russia's Voronezh region, days after a Pyongyang-made missile killed five members of a Ukrainian family.
articles.image_caption: Russian President Vladimir Putin at an official event. Ukrainian intelligence says North Korea is deploying a missile unit with up to 120 ballistic missiles to Russia's Voronezh region.
articles.nri_angle: The deepening Russia-North Korea military alliance complicates India's diplomatic balancing act between Moscow and the West, and any escalation in the conflict could further disrupt global energy prices and supply chains affecting the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran Releases First Video of Supreme Leader Khamenei Amid Growing Doubts Over His Health
articles.excerpt: A 13-second clip purportedly shows Mojtaba Khamenei teaching religious studies, but questions about its authenticity underscore deepening uncertainty over who is actually governing Iran.
articles.image_caption: Image: @htTweets via X
articles.nri_angle: Iran's leadership stability affects global oil prices and India's energy security, with implications for the millions of Indians living and working in Gulf states neighboring Iran.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Punjab CM Mann Reverses Course, Now Backs Parole for Beant Singh's Assassin
articles.excerpt: After years of opposing Jagtar Singh Hawara's release, the AAP government in Punjab has shifted its position, seeking 10-day parole for the man convicted of assassinating former Chief Minister Beant Singh.
articles.image_caption: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann addresses a gathering. The AAP government has reversed its earlier opposition to parole for Beant Singh assassination convict Jagtar Singh Hawara.
articles.nri_angle: Hawara's case resonates deeply with Sikh diaspora communities in the US, Canada, and UK, where his imprisonment is linked to the broader 1984 justice narrative.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hunter Biden Says Father's Cancer Has Spread, Calls It 'Very Painful'
articles.excerpt: In an emotional BBC interview, the former president's son revealed Joe Biden's prostate cancer has metastasized beyond his bones and acknowledged the presidential pardon was 'not good' for the country.
articles.image_caption: Hunter Biden speaks about his father's health in a BBC Newsnight interview released on August 7, 2026. Former President Joe Biden's prostate cancer has metastasized beyond his bones, according to his son.
articles.nri_angle: Major health update on a former U.S. president whose administration shaped immigration and tech policies affecting millions of Indian Americans.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: They Dreamed of Going Home to Iran. Then the Bombs Fell.
articles.excerpt: Iranian Americans who had planned to visit or return to their homeland now face an agonizing reality: a war with no clear end and family they cannot reach.
articles.image_caption: Iranian Americans who once planned to return home are now grappling with fear for family members caught in the crossfire of escalating military strikes.
articles.nri_angle: Iranian Americans who dreamed of returning to their homeland are now divided over whether the U.S. war with Iran will deliver the democratic change they sought or destroy the home they longed to return to.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Karnataka Council Chairman Basavaraj Horatti Resigns After 46-Year Legislative Career
articles.excerpt: The 80-year-old BJP leader and eight-time MLC steps down as Chairman of the Karnataka Legislative Council, ending one of Indian politics' longest legislative tenures.
articles.nri_angle: Karnataka has a significant diaspora population in U.S. tech hubs, and Horatti's departure reshapes the political landscape in their home state.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Supreme Court Orders DNA Tests, MEA Nodal Officer for Indians Killed in Russia-Ukraine War
articles.excerpt: The court directed the government to help families identify mortal remains, file compensation claims and communicate in vernacular languages, as the Centre disclosed that 51 of 219 Indians who joined Russian forces are dead or missing.
articles.nri_angle: India has 240,000 active seafarers, many from diaspora-connected families; the Supreme Court case and Black Sea attacks directly affect NRI communities with relatives in maritime service.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi Vows Campaign Against E20 Fuel as Consumer Backlash Intensifies
articles.excerpt: The Congress leader accused the government of 'stealing money and destroying lives' through mandatory ethanol blending, joining a growing chorus of opposition from transport unions, social media movements and automakers.
articles.image_caption: Rahul Gandhi has launched a national campaign against E20 ethanol-blended fuel, accusing the government of damaging consumers' vehicles.
articles.nri_angle: E20 fuel controversy affects NRI vehicle owners visiting India and highlights policy transparency concerns that mirror diaspora governance expectations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kerala Reports 105 Chikungunya Cases as Monsoon Fuels Outbreak Fears
articles.excerpt: Health authorities have intensified mosquito control across four districts as confirmed cases rise during peak monsoon season — a warning for NRIs planning trips to Kerala.
articles.image_caption: Health officials in Kerala have reported 105 confirmed chikungunya cases, with the monsoon season creating conditions for rapid Aedes mosquito breeding across several districts.
articles.nri_angle: With Onam festival season approaching, NRIs planning trips to Kerala should be aware of the outbreak and consult healthcare providers about the two FDA-approved chikungunya vaccines before traveling.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Hosts Breakfast for New NDA Allies as Coalition Nears Supermajority
articles.excerpt: Prime Minister Modi welcomed 45 newly elected Rajya Sabha MPs, including rebel Trinamool Congress lawmakers who merged with NCPI, urging them to avoid 'Delhi intrigues' and focus on governance.
articles.nri_angle: The NDA's march toward a supermajority could enable constitutional changes — including delimitation and simultaneous elections — that reshape the democratic framework Indian Americans and NRIs follow closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kejriwal Slams India's New Social Media Law Requiring Takedowns Within Three Hours
articles.excerpt: The AAP leader accuses the Modi government of using tightened IT rules to silence critics, as police file a case against Meta's India head over Facebook videos targeting the PM.
articles.nri_angle: India's social media crackdown directly affects how the diaspora engages with Indian political discourse online, while the legal action against Meta's India head raises concerns about the regulatory environment for Indian-American tech executives.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CBI Chargesheet Reveals How NTA Experts Leaked NEET Papers Using Chits and Memory
articles.excerpt: Thirteen people have been charged in the multi-state NEET-UG 2026 paper leak syndicate, with the CBI detailing how testing agency insiders memorized questions and smuggled them out on handwritten notes.
articles.image_caption: The CBI chargesheet details how NTA officials used chits and memorised answers to leak NEET-UG exam papers across multiple states.
articles.nri_angle: The NEET paper leak scandal affects thousands of Indian American families whose children prepare for the exam to pursue medical education in India, and raises questions about the integrity of India's standardized testing infrastructure.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Supreme Court Dismisses 'Cheap Publicity' Plea Seeking Criminal Probe Against Justice Varma
articles.excerpt: The bench rejected the petition calling for an FIR and SIT investigation into the unaccounted cash controversy involving Delhi High Court's former judge Yashwant Varma.
articles.image_caption: The Supreme Court of India dismissed a petition seeking a criminal probe against Justice Varma, calling it 'cheap publicity' and an abuse of the judicial process.
articles.nri_angle: The case highlights questions about judicial accountability in India, a matter closely watched by the Indian diaspora invested in the country's institutional integrity.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Assam Floods Kill 85 and Displace Over 700,000 in State's Worst Monsoon Crisis
articles.excerpt: A cloudburst in Nagaland triggered devastating flooding across Upper Assam's Brahmaputra Valley, submerging nearly 900 villages and destroying 37,000 hectares of cropland.
articles.image_caption: Floodwaters inundated villages across Upper Assam after heavy monsoon rainfall swelled the Brahmaputra and its tributaries beyond danger levels. Rescue operations evacuated thousands from submerged areas in Sivasagar and Charaideo districts.
articles.nri_angle: The floods have devastated communities in Assam with deep ties to the diaspora, prompting relief campaigns from Indian-Americans and raising questions about the pace of flood-control infrastructure investment in the Northeast.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Americans Still Need $110,000 to Afford the Typical Home as Affordability Barely Budges
articles.excerpt: A new Redfin report finds the income required to buy the median U.S. home has stayed near record highs, leaving the typical household $22,000 short.
articles.nri_angle: Indian American households earn above the national median but are concentrated in the least affordable metros like San Francisco and San Jose, where housing costs often exceed even high tech salaries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New Mexico Court Orders Meta to Pay $942 Million in Landmark Child Safety Ruling
articles.excerpt: A judge added $567 million in abatement costs on top of the earlier $375 million jury verdict, making it the largest child safety penalty against a social media company.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian American parents, the ruling underscores growing legal momentum to hold social media platforms accountable for child safety and could influence how their children use these platforms.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi High Court Orders Takedown of Vulgar Content Exploiting PhysicsWallah Founder's Identity
articles.excerpt: Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani grants interim injunction protecting Alakh Pandey's personality rights, directing Google, Meta, X, and Telegram to remove sexually explicit and impersonation content.
articles.image_caption: Alakh Pandey, founder of edtech platform PhysicsWallah. The Delhi High Court ordered the removal of vulgar deepfake content exploiting his identity.
articles.nri_angle: The ruling highlights evolving digital identity protections in Indian law, relevant as Indian-origin content creators face cross-border misuse of their likenesses.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Emerging Markets Learn a Painful Lesson as AI Tech Hype Unravels
articles.excerpt: South Korea's KOSPI lost 40% in six weeks and volatility surpassed COVID-era peaks as AI-fueled concentration turned once-diversified emerging market indexes into ground zero for the global tech selloff.
articles.image_caption: Samsung Electronics, a bellwether for Asian tech markets, has seen its stock slide amid weakening AI chip demand and rising geopolitical uncertainty.
articles.nri_angle: India is emerging as an unlikely beneficiary of the AI selloff, with foreign investors rotating back into Indian equities after months of outflows, making the country's 'anti-AI' trade status a potential advantage for diaspora investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How the Iran War Exposed China's New Oil Weapon: Clean Energy Dominance
articles.excerpt: As the Strait of Hormuz closure disrupts global crude supplies, China's EV boom and clean tech exports are reshaping energy geopolitics — with major implications for India.
articles.nri_angle: India's energy security is being reshaped as the Hormuz crisis forces a choice between costly oil imports and growing dependence on Chinese clean technology.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Measles-Infected Visitor Spent 11 Hours at Universal Studios Hollywood, Triggering Health Alert
articles.excerpt: Los Angeles County officials warn anyone who visited the theme park on July 26 may have been exposed as the U.S. records its highest measles count since 1991.
articles.nri_angle: Universal Studios Hollywood is a top destination for Indian tourists visiting Southern California, and the exposure alert is relevant for recent visitors from the diaspora community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran Warns Gulf States of Retaliation Against Energy Sites If U.S. Strikes Resume
articles.excerpt: Tehran delivered the threat through diplomatic channels to Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Turkey, and Pakistan after Trump warned of hitting Iran's energy infrastructure, putting Gulf allies in a bind between Washington and Tehran.
articles.nri_angle: Nine million Indian nationals in the Gulf face direct risk; India imports 60% of its crude from Gulf producers, making any infrastructure strikes an immediate economic concern.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chandipura Virus Death Toll Passes 80 as India Deploys National Response Team
articles.excerpt: The largest Chandipura outbreak in two decades has killed at least 82 people, mostly children, prompting India to send a national emergency team to Gujarat as the monsoon season fuels sandfly transmission.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs traveling to India during monsoon season, especially to rural Gujarat, Rajasthan, or Maharashtra, should take sandfly precautions and seek immediate medical care for children with sudden fevers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Drug-Resistant Superbug Candida Auris Tops 3,000 Cases Across 23 U.S. States
articles.excerpt: The deadly fungus, which can resist last-resort antifungal medications, is spreading through hospitals and nursing homes at an accelerating pace, with Texas, Michigan, and Illinois reporting the highest caseloads.
articles.nri_angle: Indian American families with elderly relatives in nursing homes or family members in extended hospital stays should be aware of facility-level C. auris protocols.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Lok Sabha Passes Bill Recognizing Digital Bank Records as Court Evidence
articles.excerpt: The Bankers' Books Evidence Bill 2026 replaces a 135-year-old colonial-era law, giving electronic banking records full legal standing in Indian courts for the first time.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who manage Indian bank accounts entirely online will benefit from clearer legal standing of their digital banking records in Indian courts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Gas to Stone: How Scientists Are Turning Carbon Dioxide Into Rock
articles.excerpt: Researchers in Iceland, MIT, and South Korea are advancing carbon mineralization technologies that convert CO2 into solid minerals, offering permanent climate storage solutions.
articles.nri_angle: Indian researchers at institutions including IIT and TERI are studying basalt formations in the Deccan Traps — one of the world's largest volcanic rock formations — as potential carbon storage sites.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Sounds Alarm on Dengue Surge as Monsoon Fuels Record Early-Season Cases
articles.excerpt: With nearly 7,000 dengue cases recorded by February alone and multiple states reporting spikes, the government is rushing to bolster surveillance before the monsoon peak.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs travelling to India during monsoon season face an expanding dengue transmission window that now extends well beyond traditional post-monsoon months.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: When Wildfires Make Their Own Weather: France Records First-Ever Fire Thunderstorm
articles.excerpt: A wildfire near Bordeaux generated a pyrocumulonimbus cloud that created lightning and ignited new fires — a phenomenon never before seen in France.
articles.nri_angle: The escalating European wildfire crisis affects Indian diaspora communities across France and Spain, disrupting travel and tourism during peak season.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Supreme Court Orders Release of Minors, Bars Coercive Action as NEET Crisis Deepens
articles.excerpt: The bench warned against police excesses against student protesters and may constitute an SIT led by a former SC judge to probe brutality allegations.
articles.nri_angle: Indian parents abroad closely track NEET developments as the exam remains the gateway for medical education in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Across the Line of Control, Two Kashmirs Diverge Sharply
articles.excerpt: India's Jammu and Kashmir is drawing record tourists and launching startups, while Pakistan-occupied Kashmir struggles with inflation, repression, and crumbling infrastructure.
articles.nri_angle: For Kashmiri diaspora communities split by the LoC, the widening development gap raises urgent questions about the future of cross-border family ties and the region's political trajectory.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Gen Z Storms the Streets but Remains Invisible in Parliament
articles.excerpt: The 'Cockroach' protest movement forced a cabinet minister's resignation, yet Indians under 35 hold barely any seats in the legislatures that govern them.
articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora families watching their siblings and cousins spend years and fortunes on exam coaching that leads nowhere, raising questions about whether India's merit-based mobility promise still holds.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Russia Expands Power to Seize Property of Citizens Abroad Under Sweeping New Law
articles.excerpt: Federal Law 168-FZ, signed by Putin and taking effect September 1, vastly broadens extraterritorial prosecution of Russians overseas, enabling courts to freeze bank accounts and seize property without the accused being present or even notified.
articles.nri_angle: Russian-speaking diaspora members, including those in India and South Asia, who retain property or bank accounts in Russia face asset seizure for speech deemed anti-state under the new law.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Completes $55 Billion EA Takeover in Largest Leveraged Buyout Ever
articles.excerpt: The Public Investment Fund now owns 93.4% of Electronic Arts after clearing all regulatory hurdles, with Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners holding a 1.1% stake in the gaming giant.
articles.nri_angle: Indian gamers and the large Indian diaspora tech workforce in the U.S. may feel the effects as EA navigates its new ownership structure, particularly if cost-cutting measures impact the company's studios or workforce.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Armed Man With Weapons Cache Arrested at Trump Golf Course Before Presidential Visit
articles.excerpt: Jeanine John Taele, 38, was found monitoring security preparations at Trump National Golf Club in Rancho Palos Verdes, days before the president's scheduled dinner there.
articles.nri_angle: The incident at Trump's California golf club underscores ongoing security concerns at high-profile presidential venues, relevant as Indian-Americans increasingly attend political fundraisers and events hosted at such locations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Cracks Down on GLP-1 Weight-Loss Drugs With Supply Chain Sweep
articles.excerpt: India's drug regulator has inspected 49 entities and banned surrogate advertising of semaglutide-based weight-loss drugs as cheap generics flood the market after patent expiry.
articles.image_caption: India has launched a nationwide crackdown on unregulated GLP-1 weight-loss drugs including semaglutide
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora members seeking cheaper GLP-1 drugs during India visits should be aware that only specialist-prescribed purchases are legal; buying from wellness clinics or online pharmacies without a valid prescription could carry legal risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Russia Turns Ukraine's Gas Stations Into Deadly Targets in Escalating Drone War
articles.excerpt: Over 200 fuel stations have been hit in two months as Moscow retaliates for Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries that have triggered fuel shortages from Crimea to Siberia.
articles.image_caption: A Ukrainian gas station damaged by a Russian drone strike
articles.nri_angle: The tit-for-tat energy infrastructure attacks have contributed to global oil price volatility, directly affecting Indian energy import costs and shipping routes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India’s Auto Parts Industry Admits E20 Fuel May Demand New Materials
articles.excerpt: Component makers acknowledge the ethanol blend could force material upgrades, as a resurfaced government study shows degradation in fuel-system plastics and rubber parts.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with vehicles in India or sending money for family vehicle expenses face direct impact from E20-related repair costs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Keeps Making Threats but the World Has Stopped Flinching
articles.excerpt: After months of dramatic ultimatums that rarely materialize, allies and adversaries alike are treating Trump's escalating rhetoric as background noise rather than genuine threats.
articles.image_caption: Trump at a press conference
articles.nri_angle: The credibility gap in US foreign policy directly affects Indian energy security, Gulf shipping routes, and the strategic calculus of the India-US relationship.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
